test_cases.title: Verify normal behavior for Overpressure Protection
test_cases.description:
Check that the device follows the requirements described in section 4.1: If cuﬀ pressure exceeds 299 mmHg at any point, or exceeds 300 mmHg
for longer than 3 seconds due to sensor fault, the device immediately
triggers an emergency deﬂation valve, halting inﬂation and venting the
cuﬀ within 2 seconds, independent of the main ﬁrmware control loop.

test_cases.title: Verify boundary conditions for Overpressure Protection
test_cases.description:
Test the stated limits and boundary conditions described in section 4.1: If cuﬀ pressure exceeds 299 mmHg at any point, or exceeds 300 mmHg
for longer than 3 seconds due to sensor fault, the device immediately
triggers an emergency deﬂation valve, halting inﬂation and venting the
cuﬀ within 2 seconds, independent of the main ﬁrmware control loop.

test_cases.title: Verify error handling for Overpressure Protection
test_cases.description:
Check the device response to invalid, abnormal, or failure conditions described in section 4.1: If cuﬀ pressure exceeds 299 mmHg at any point, or exceeds 300 mmHg
for longer than 3 seconds due to sensor fault, the device immediately
triggers an emergency deﬂation valve, halting inﬂation and venting the
cuﬀ within 2 seconds, independent of the main ﬁrmware control loop.

test_cases.title: Verify normal behavior for Alarm Thresholds
test_cases.description:
Check that the device follows the requirements described in section 4.3: The device does not sound an audible alarm for elevated readings by
default; audible alarms are limited to the E1–E5 error conditions above
and are user‑conﬁgurable in the settings menu, except for E3
(overpressure), which cannot be silenced for safety reasons.
